summary: In this excerpt from a novel ("Book 3 — part 20"), the narrator discusses a baby's adoption with Dr. Hannah Klein, who doubts the adoption was as easy as claimed and is skeptical of the Children of Light organization and of Dr. Alex Goddard, an alternative-medicine doctor who now provides children for adoption. Klein warns the narrator to stay away and gives her a list of adoption agencies. The narrator's pager then shows a page from Lou Crenshaw, a security guard, who may have news from Lenox Hill about Sarah, interrupting the conversation.
one_line: In a fiction excerpt, the narrator questions a doctor about the Children of Light adoption and Dr. Alex Goddard, then rushes off after a page about Sarah.
key_facts: Dr. Hannah Klein says the adoption process as described sounds 'most exceptional' and 'actually more like impossible.'
Klein suspects the child may have been kidnapped or something, given how easily the adoption supposedly went.
The narrator says the organization that obtained the baby is called Children of Light, believed to be up the Hudson somewhere, past the Cloisters.
Klein describes the Children of Light as 'All that so-called New Age.'
Klein says Alex Goddard's supporters offer only hearsay and that his success is anecdotal, which she attributes to the 'placebo effect.'
Klein says she is not even sure Alex Goddard is board-certified.
Klein warns that people like Goddard, 'Oftentimes, ... do more harm than good.'
Klein asks when Alex Goddard started providing children for adoption, calling it 'peculiar.'
The narrator's pager shows a number belonging to Lou Crenshaw, the security guard, who had been off duty that day.
The narrator believes Crenshaw would only page her about news from Lenox Hill, possibly about Sarah.
Klein gives the narrator a list of adoption agencies, saying she has dealt with some of them through letters of reference for patients.
Klein squeezes the narrator's hand, the closest the two women had come to intimacy.
